Based on my review of the fleet snapshot, here is what I consider worth your attention.

## 1. Open exception on `rese-a-inv` — needs resolution
There is one open exception, opened 2026-04-03, on the reservation worker `rese-a-inv`: `PermissionError: append_to_reservations`. This is the single `not_ok` run in recent history (419 ok / 1 not_ok) and the one `effects_not_applied` this period. The effect stage stoppage count is 1, matching this. The previous period had zero effects-not-applied, so this is a regression. It looks like a permissions/credentials issue on the reservations side rather than a logic bug — worth having the operator verify the reservation store credentials/ACLs for that worker and clear the exception.

## 2. Effects success rate dropped period-over-period
- Previous period: 3/3 effects applied, 3 verified.
- This period: 3 attempted, 2 applied, 2 verified — one effect failed (the `rese-a-inv` case above).

Volume, arrivals, claims, acceptances and refusals are otherwise identical period-over-period, so the only operational change is this one failed effect. Fixing the reservation exception should restore the effect/verification line to parity.

## 3. Refusals are stable but non-trivial
17 refusals out of 420 arrivals (~4.0%) in both periods, all stopping at the decision stage. This is consistent, not a spike, but it is the largest stoppage category by far (17 decision stoppages vs 1 effect). If these refusals are expected policy rejections that is fine; if any are unexpected, the decision-stage refusal breakdown (available via `compare_periods`) is the place to look. No customer-level refusal spike is indicated in the snapshot.

## 4. Three enrichment promotions this period, zero confirmations logged
`enri-a-05`, `enri-a-11`, and `enri-a-23` were promoted this period (previous period had none). However, `confirmations_logged_this_period` is 0. With three fresh promotions and no confirmations recorded, I would want the operator to confirm whether these promotions have actually been validated/confirmed in production, or whether the confirmation step is being skipped. This is especially important given item 5 below.

## 5. Dependency concentration — single engine for 85.7% of the fleet
The established measurement flags a high dependency concentration:
- Engine `enrichment/harness/execute_enrichment.py` is used by **60 of 70 workers (85.7% fleet share)**.
- This is also the top shared dependency fleet-wide.

This is the dominant structural risk in the fleet. The 60 enrichment workers all depend on one engine, so any change to that engine has an 85% blast radius. Combined with the fact that three enrichment workers were just promoted and no confirmations were logged, I recommend the operator treat any change to `execute_enrichment.py` as high-risk and ensure it goes through canary/confirmation before broad rollout.

I have recorded an improvement proposal (SUG-001) suggesting a versioned or parallel enrichment harness to reduce this blast radius.

## 6. Workload shape
Task distribution is heavily enrichment-dominated (60 enrichment vs 4 aggregation, 3 reconciliation, 3 reservation). Customer distribution is balanced (11–12 per scope). No row spike is indicated. The fleet is effectively an enrichment-processing fleet, which is why the single enrichment engine concentration matters so much.

## Suggested operator actions
1. Resolve the `rese-a-inv` `PermissionError: append_to_reservations` — check reservation-store credentials/ACLs, then clear the exception.
2. Verify whether the three enrichment promotions (`enri-a-05/11/23`) were actually confirmed; if confirmations are required, ensure they are logged.
3. Treat `enrichment/harness/execute_enrichment.py` as a critical shared dependency — gate changes to it behind canary/confirmation given its 85.7% fleet share.
4. Consider the recorded improvement proposal (SUG-001) to reduce engine concentration.

No changes have been made to the fleet; the above is read-only analysis and recommendations.
